note_claims.claim: The patient is presenting with dysuria and urinary frequency for 3 days.
The patient reports dysuria and frequency (about every 30 minutes) since Saturday.
The patient reports possible pink-tinged urine this morning.
The patient reports loin pain and fever.
The patient reports no rigors, nausea, or vomiting.
The patient reports no vaginal discharge or itching.
The patient has a history of one previous UTI two years ago, treated with antibiotics (agent unknown).
The patient has no known renal disease.
The patient takes Vitamin D in the winter.
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The examination was a telephone consultation, and the patient speaks comfortably in full sentences and sounds well.
The clinical impression is a lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).
Possible early pregnancy is noted and needs to be excluded.
The prescribed treatment is nitrofurantoin 100 mg modified-release capsules, twice a day for seven days.
A pregnancy test is ordered today.
A urine sample is required for culture before starting antibiotics.
The patient must ring back tomorrow with the pregnancy test result.
If the pregnancy test is positive, a face-to-face review and treatment plan revision will occur.
The patient is advised to drink plenty of fluids and take paracetamol for discomfort.
Ibuprofen should be avoided until pregnancy is excluded.
The patient should call the practice or 111 immediately if they develop pain in their back or side, a fever, shivering, or vomiting.
The patient should call back if they do not start to feel better within 48 hours of starting antibiotics or if their condition worsens.
